body.input: Which companies announced expanding into the Nordics in 2026?

response.content:
Here are companies that announced expansions into the Nordic region in 2026, based on available reports:

## Technology & Fintech

- **Revolut** — Announced plans to expand further into the Nordics with a new branch in Sweden, offering local IBANs, clearing numbers, and Swedish-format account numbers. The company is also recruiting for positions across Norway, Denmark, and Finland, aiming to reach 3 million Swedish customers by 2030.

- **Binance** — Partnered with Sweden-based Scrive for expansion into the Nordics and Benelux, using Scrive's eID Hub for secure identification and KYC processes, starting with Sweden and Denmark.

- **Bottomline** — Partnered with Swedish firm Knowit to bring its financial technology solutions for business payments and financial messaging to the Nordic market.

- **Intergiro** — The Sweden-based fintech launched its Banking as a Service (BaaS) platform, Intergiro.3d, in Finland.

- **BE-terna** — The pan-European cloud and IT services firm acquired Swedish Microsoft partner Tydab to establish its first offices in Scandinavia, marking the start of its Nordics market penetration.

## Pharma & Healthcare

- **GENESIS Pharma** — Expanded its partnership with Alnylam Pharmaceuticals into four Nordic markets (Denmark, Finland, Norway, and Sweden), adding these to its existing 13 Southeastern European markets for the commercialisation of RNAi therapies.

## Consumer & Skincare

- **Kao (Curél brand)** — Japan's leading skincare brand Curél launched in the Nordics as part of Kao's broader EMEA skincare growth strategy, backed by its biomimetic ceramide technology.

## Media & Entertainment

- **Studiocanal** — Acquired a majority stake in Danish production company Sam Productions (in June 2026) with plans to expand across the Nordics, consolidating operations in Denmark, Sweden, and Norway under a single entity.

- **Agillic** — Aller Media, the Nordic magazine leader, rolled out the Agillic marketing platform to Finland, Norway, and Sweden to replicate its success from Denmark.

## Travel & Mobility

- **Gray Dawes Group** — Expanded its Nordic reach through a strategic partnership with Berg-Hansen, combining the latter's Nordic expertise with Gray Dawes' international operations.

- **iCabbi** (Mobilize/Renault subsidiary) — Continued its Nordic expansion into Sweden, Norway, and Denmark through its partnership with Cabonline, the largest taxi company in the Nordics.

## Data Centres & Infrastructure

- **atNorth** — The Icelandic data-centre company is developing SWE04, a large-scale AI and HPC data-centre campus in Sollefteå, Sweden, with 300 MW of planned capacity.

## Fund Management

- **Kraft Finans** — The Norwegian fund manager expanded into Sweden, marketing additional funds including a Norwegian equity fund and a global fund-of-funds.

- **Mandatum** — Plans to expand its product range beyond fixed income in the Nordic market.

---

*Note: The iCabbi–Cabonline partnership was originally announced in late 2022 but continued its operational rollout across the Nordics in subsequent years. Some entries (e.g., BE-terna/Tydab) may reflect announcements from earlier in the year with ongoing 2026 execution.*

## User account menu. ## User account menu. ## Breadcrumb. 3. BE-terna Makes Dynamics Acquisition To Start Nordics Expansion. # BE-terna makes Dynamics acquisition to start Nordics expansion. Pan-European cloud and IT services firm BE-terna has acquired Tydab, a Swedish Microsoft partner specialising in Dynamics 365 finance and supply chain management. Last Ocotober, BE-terna acquired another Dynamics specialist in Pipol, an international provider of Dynamics business solutions. Tydab is headquartered in Halmstad with offices in Stockholm and Helsingborg, and will provide BE-terna with its first offices in Scandinavia to add to the ones it has in Austria, Germany, Switzerland and across the Baltics. Christian Kranebitter, CEO of BE-terna Group, said: “Tydab's Microsoft Dynamics 365 technology know-how is really impressive. The company covers the entire value chain of manufacturing, trade and retail companies and is a highly reliable partner for complex implementation projects in these sectors.”. He said: “With Tydab we now have a strong footprint in the Swedish market, which is the first step of our future Nordics market penetration journey. We also believe the typically Scandinavian innovative nature of Tydab will spill over to the entire BE-terna Group.”. Henrik Mathiasson, managing director at Tydab, said: “Together with BE-terna we will be able to significantly expand our position in the Scandinavian market and will also have a broader technological base in the future.”. The value of the latest BE-terna acquisition has not been disclosed. ## Share. Dave Bishop, Chief Operating Officer at Gray Dawes Group, said the partnership was intended to strengthen the company’s ability to support clients in key markets rather than simply expand its international footprint.

“Delivering a genuinely global travel management proposition means having the right people, expertise and service capabilities in the markets that matter to our clients,” he said.

“Berg-Hansen has an established reputation, deep local knowledge and a service-led approach that aligns closely with our own. By combining their Nordic expertise with our own international operations and existing partner relationships, we can offer clients greater geographical reach while maintaining the quality of service they expect from Gray Dawes.” [...] Bishop also suggested the partnership reflects wider changes taking place within the industry following the acquisition of CWT by American Express Global Business Travel.

“We also see an opportunity to bring together other TMCs that may be reassessing their international partnerships as a result of the ongoing consolidation in our industry,” he said.

Suzanne Horner, Chief Executive Officer of Gray Dawes Group, said the deal reflected growing demand from clients for international support without sacrificing local expertise and personal service. [...] “The corporate travel management sector is evolving rapidly,” she said. “Consolidation is reshaping the competitive landscape, while clients continue to look for providers that can support their international ambitions without losing the personal relationships and accountability that make a real difference.”

Horner added that the company sees opportunities for independent TMCs to collaborate more closely while retaining their individual identities and local strengths.

For Berg-Hansen, the partnership provides access to Gray Dawes’ international network while allowing it to support clients requiring broader geographic coverage.

Title: Dublin’s iCabbi continues Nordic expansion with Cabonline deal
# Dublin’s iCabbi continues Nordic expansion with Cabonline deal. From left: iCabbi co-founders Bob Nixon, Gavan Walsh and Niall O’Callaghan. The company provides a cloud-based dispatch tech platform that enables taxi companies to automate and optimise their operations. Irish tech company iCabbi continues its expansion into the Nordics, upping operations in Finland, and breaking ground in Sweden, Norway, and Denmark, after winning its bid to provide taxi booking and dispatch technology solutions to the largest taxi company in the region, Cabonline. Established back in 2009, iCabbi has expanded into the largest dispatch technology provider in the world, powering approximately 100,000 taxis every day in Ireland, the UK, the US, Canada, New Zealand, Australia and Finland, where it competes with major global rideshare players like FreeNow and Uber. It provides a fully cloud-based dispatch taxi technology platform that enables taxi companies to automate, optimise and grow their operations. Further iCabbi expansion into Europe will take place in the coming months starting with the Netherlands and Italy. “iCabbi is delighted to be chosen as the technology partner of choice by the largest taxi operator in the Nordics, Cabonline,” said iCabbi CEO and co-founder Gavan Walsh. “We’re both ambitious companies, looking to push the boundaries of efficiency, innovation and scale for taxi and mobility services.”. iCabbi announced it had processed 1bn bookings on its platform earlier this month. The company has significant R&D investments planned, which will see its product innovation team grow by 50 people over the next 18 months. Speaking to Silicon Republic’s Ann O’Dea at Slush in November, Walsh said that while taxi is a local business, taxi companies need “world-class technology to meet passenger expectations”. “That’s what iCabbi gives our customers, tools to compete, and we’re constantly striving to find ways to make taxi companies better and better.”.
